title: Qualys CI Lookup Rules
subtitle: How a scanned host finds its CI

bullets.title: Contract.
bullets.detail: process(rule, sourceValue, sourcePayload) returns one sys_id or null. sourceValue is the rule's source field (SERIAL_NUMBER, DNS or IP); the OS, DNS and IP come from the payload.

bullets.title: Normalisation.
bullets.detail: The value is coerced to a string and trimmed; names are lower-cased; the text before the first dot is the short host; an absent DNS or OS reads as empty, never as the string "undefined".

bullets.title: Ignored classes.
bullets.detail: The framework's _ignoreClass, else sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass, added as sys_class_name NOT IN on every search. Exact class names, no hierarchy.

bullets.title: Exactly one.
bullets.detail: query() with no setLimit, then next() and hasNext(): a second row declines. The rules that walk records count distinct owning CIs instead, and two owners decline.

bullets.title: Address tie-break.
bullets.detail: Only the FQDN, host name with domain, layered DNS and device name rules break several candidates with the scanned IP. The address rules never tie-break.

bullets.title: Loopback and link-local.
bullets.detail: The address and virtual server rules refuse 127. and 169.254. before reading anything else.

bullets.title: Retired records.
bullets.detail: retired(): install_status 7, operational_status 6 or life cycle stage Retired. The virtual server rules set a retired twin aside; the platform property filterOutDecommissionedCI drops retired CIs after any rule.

bullets.title: classFor(OS).
bullets.detail: Lower-cased OS text; three or more "/"-separated guesses give no class. Keywords in order, first hit wins: esx; windows (with server) / windows; aix; solaris, sunos; hp-ux; netapp, ontap; printer, laserjet, jetdirect; red hat, linux, centos, ubuntu, suse, debian, fedora, euleros, oracle enterprise, amazon; nx-os, catos, cisco.

bullets.title: Classes.
bullets.detail: ESX Server, Windows Server or Computer, AIX Server, Solaris Server, HP-UX Server, Storage Server, Printer, Linux Server, Network Gear. Anything else: no class.

bullets.title: Class rules.
bullets.detail: Search the OS class and its sub-classes only, and decline without a class. Hardware rules search the whole cmdb_ci_hardware tree and keep the OS class as a preference.

bullets.title: Class agreement.
bullets.detail: agrees(cls): the CI class equals the OS class, sits beneath it or above it (parentsOf through sys_db_object.super_class). A Cisco IOS router therefore never lands on a Computer.

bullets.title: Appliances.
bullets.detail: In Layered DNS Match and Hostname Hardware Match a Linux fingerprint also agrees with Network Gear, Load Balancer and Storage Server records, because appliances answer scans as Linux.

bullets.title: Load balancer devices.
bullets.detail: A cmdb_ci_lb record is never accepted as the host behind a name or an address; the virtual server rules handle those addresses instead.

bullets.title: Host name agreement.
bullets.detail: The IP rules also require the CI's first name label to equal the scanned label, or to differ from it only by a hyphenated suffix such as -mgmt.

concepts.title: The signs the scripts look for

bullets.title: Placeholder serials.
bullets.detail: Refused when shorter than four characters or one of: 0, none, n/a, na, unknown, empty, not specified, not available, no serial, default string, to be filled by o.e.m., system serial number, chassis serial number, 0123456789, 1234567890.

bullets.title: Cisco phones.
bullets.detail: DNS label ^sep([0-9a-f]{12})$: the twelve hex characters are the MAC, rebuilt in four spellings (64:F6:9D:D5:C9:B0, lower case, 64F69DD5C9B0, lower case). Search: a network adapter with that MAC owned by an IP Phone, then the phone's own mac_address, then the Unified CM device name SEP... in upper case.

bullets.title: Other phones and scanners.
bullets.detail: No MAC in the name (Avaya avx... stations, scanners). The host label is searched by name in IP Phone and Imaging Hardware only, outside the hardware tree. Declined when the OS gives a server or desktop class (Linux excepted) unless the OS text says phone; several hits: the one on the scanned address.

bullets.title: Management controllers.
bullets.detail: Label tail after the last hyphen in ilo, ilom, idrac, drac, ipmi, bmc, oob, mgmt, imm, cimc, rmm, con, or OS text with ilo, ilom, idrac, drac, remote access controller, imm, cimc, bmc, ipmi, lights out. The label before the hyphen is the server name, searched hardware-wide; a load balancer device is refused.

bullets.title: Network interfaces.
bullets.detail: DNS in a .network. domain, or a hyphen segment that is an interface marker: vlan, v, hsrp, vrrp, po, eth, gi, te, lo, mgmt, aom, vs, fab, whole or followed by digits. Prefixes are tried longest first on Network Gear and Load Balancer devices; two hits decline.

bullets.title: Virtual server sign.
bullets.detail: OS text with f5, big-ip, big ip or netscaler, or a label segment vip or vs (vip, vip2, ...-vip, vs1). Load Balancer Service searched on fqdn, then name, then the label, then ip_address.

bullets.title: Twins.
bullets.detail: Several service records of one name are one virtual server recorded more than once (HA pair, test copy): kept to the one on the scanned address, then the live one. Two different names decline.

bullets.title: Member rule.
bullets.detail: Service to pools to pool members through cmdb_rel_ci, each member to its server record (in cmdb_ci_hardware, not ignored, not a balancer). One machine behind every member returns the server; a member the CMDB cannot place, several machines or two live records of one machine decline.

bullets.title: Service rule.
bullets.detail: Never reads the pool. Attaches the one live virtual server record; two live twins decline.

bullets.title: Names.
bullets.detail: FQDN rules: the whole dotted name on fqdn. FQDN Name rules: the whole dotted name on the name field. Host name rules: the first label on name. Domain rules: the first label on name and the rest on dns_domain. A bare label without a dot declines the FQDN rules.

bullets.title: Addresses.
bullets.detail: ip_address on the OS class, then on the hardware tree; then the adapter walk (cmdb_ci_network_adapter.ip_address to cmdb_ci) and the IP Address record walk (cmdb_ci_ip_address to nic.cmdb_ci), distinct owners counted, class and host name agreement on the one owner.

bullets.title: Last resort.
bullets.detail: FQDN Name Broad Match searches the whole cmdb_ci table by name when everything else declined, still one record only.

The sys_id of the single CI of the OS-implied class (sub-classes included, ignored classes excluded) whose name equals the short hostname; null in every other case.

The sys_id of the one cmdb_ci_ip_phone or cmdb_ci_imaging_hardware record (sub-classes included, ignored classes excluded) whose name equals the host label; when several carry the name, the single one whose ip_address equals the scanned IP. null otherwise, and null when the OS names a server, desktop or other classed system.

Source field DNS (sourceValue). Payload field OS (sourcePayload.OS), lower-cased, empty when absent, used only for the controller marker words. IP and SERIAL_NUMBER are not read.

The sys_id of the one record of cmdb_ci_hardware or any class beneath it (outside sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass and not a cmdb_ci_lb record or a class beneath cmdb_ci_lb) whose name equals the label with its last hyphen segment removed; null in every other case.
Network Interface Name Match
Source field DNS (sourceValue) only. The header says the OS is also read from sourcePayload, but the code never references sourcePayload: no OS, IP or SERIAL_NUMBER value takes part in the match.

The sys_id of the one record of cmdb_ci_netgear or cmdb_ci_lb, or any class beneath them, outside sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass, whose name equals the longest hyphen-joined prefix of the label that names anything at all; null in every other case.
FQDN Name Hardware Match
Source field DNS (sourceValue). No payload field is read: neither IP nor OS influences the result.
The sys_id of the single hardware CI whose name equals the scanned FQDN; null when none or more than one carries it.
Load Balancer Member Match
Source field IP (sourceValue); payload fields DNS and OS from sourcePayload; the framework variable _ignoreClass when it is passed, else the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass.
The sys_id of the one cmdb_ci_hardware record behind the virtual server (the single live record when that machine is recorded more than once under one name); otherwise null.
Load Balancer Service Match
Source field IP (sourceValue); payload fields DNS and OS from sourcePayload; the framework variable _ignoreClass when it is passed, else the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass.
The sys_id of the one cmdb_ci_lb_service record left after narrowing by scanned address and then by live status; otherwise null.
IP Class Match
Source field IP (sourceValue). Payload fields: OS (class choice through classFor) and DNS (host-name agreement). The rule argument is never read.
The sys_id of the single CI of the OS-implied class whose ip_address equals the trimmed scanned address and whose name agrees with the scanned DNS label; null in every other case.
IP Hardware Match
Source field IP (sourceValue). Payload fields: OS (class preference consumed only by agrees()) and DNS (host-name agreement). The rule argument is never read.

The sys_id of the one cmdb_ci_hardware row (any sub-class outside the ignore list) whose ip_address equals the scanned address, provided it is not in cmdb_ci_lb, its name agrees with the scanned label and its class agrees with the OS-implied class; null otherwise.
IP Adapter Match
Source field IP (sourceValue). Payload fields: OS (class preference consumed by agrees() inside the owner loop) and DNS (host-name agreement). The rule argument is never read.

The sys_id of the single CI (counted once however many of its adapters carry the address) owning an adapter with the scanned ip_address, when its class agrees with the OS, it is not a cmdb_ci_lb row and its name agrees with the scanned label; null otherwise.
IP Layered Match
Source field IP (sourceValue). Payload fields: OS (class preference consumed by agrees() inside the owner loop) and DNS (host-name agreement). The rule argument is never read.

The sys_id of the single CI at the end of cmdb_ci_ip_address -> nic (cmdb_ci_network_adapter) -> cmdb_ci, counted once across its address records, when its class agrees with the OS, it is not in cmdb_ci_lb and its name agrees with the scanned label; null otherwise.
FQDN Name Broad Match
Source field DNS (sourceValue). No payload field is read: neither IP nor OS influences the result.
The sys_id of the single cmdb_ci row, in any class not on the ignore list, whose name equals the scanned FQDN; null when none or the name is shared.

rules.name: USEM Serial Number Class Match
rules.purpose: Trusts the Qualys SERIAL_NUMBER, the one identifier that stays with a machine while names and addresses get reused, but only inside the CMDB class the scanned OS text points at, so a Red Hat host can land only on a Linux Server and a Windows Server carrying the same serial is never seen. It opens the chain because a unique serial inside the right class is the strongest evidence the feed offers.
rules.reads: SERIAL_NUMBER (sourceValue) plus sourcePayload.OS; the IP and DNS fields are not read.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the single CI in the OS-implied class (sub-classes included, ignored classes excluded) whose serial_number equals the trimmed serial; null in every other case.
rules.before: Nothing custom runs before it; it is the first rule of the chain, so every host that reports a serial reaches it (in this feed the Cloud Agent hosts; unauthenticated network scans rarely carry one).
rules.after: USEM Serial Number Hardware Match

mechanics.title: Empty serial guard.
mechanics.detail: If sourceValue is empty (null, undefined or an empty string) the script returns null at once; nothing else in the payload is read.

mechanics.title: Trim the serial.
mechanics.detail: sourceValue is coerced to a string and trimmed; that trimmed value, with its case unchanged, is the value the search uses. Sample: 'VMware-42 1a 9c 3f 7d 2e 61 b8-55 04 e2 91 6a 27 c3 08' passes through untouched.

mechanics.title: Placeholder and length guard.
mechanics.detail: A serial shorter than four characters is refused, and so is one whose lower-cased form, wrapped in commas, is found in the placeholder list quoted in full under literals, because such vendor values sit on dozens of CIs.

mechanics.title: Resolve the ignored classes.
mechanics.detail: If the framework defined a non-empty _ignoreClass variable its string value is used; otherwise the script reads gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). An empty result means no class filter is added to the query.

mechanics.title: Class from the OS.
mechanics.detail: classFor(sourcePayload.OS) casts the OS to a lower-cased string; more than two '/'-separated parts gives no class; else the first keyword hit in order (esx, windows, aix, solaris, hp-ux, netapp, printer, linux, cisco) names the class. No class: null.

mechanics.title: Open the class table.
mechanics.detail: A GlideRecord is opened on the class chosen; its sub-classes come along by table inheritance. If gr.isValid() is false the class is not installed on the instance and the rule returns null.

mechanics.title: Query the serial inside the class.
mechanics.detail: addQuery('serial_number', serial) as an exact match, plus addQuery('sys_class_name', 'NOT IN', ignore) when the ignore list is non-empty; then query() with no setLimit.

mechanics.title: Exactly one row.
mechanics.detail: If next() is false the rule returns null. The first row's getUniqueValue() is held; if hasNext() is true a second CI in the class carries the same serial (cloned VM, serial typed on the wrong record) and the rule returns null; else the held sys_id is returned.

declines: sourceValue is empty
the trimmed serial is shorter than four characters
the lower-cased serial is one of the placeholder tokens in the junk list
sourcePayload.OS is empty or contains none of the classFor keywords
the OS text holds three or more '/'-separated guesses (split('/').length > 2)
the class table named by classFor is not valid on the instance (gr.isValid() false)
no CI in that class (sub-classes included, ignored classes excluded) carries the serial
two or more CIs in that class carry the serial (hasNext() true), whatever their state, class depth or address

rules.sibling: Unlike USEM Serial Number Hardware Match it reads sourcePayload.OS, derives a class with classFor, searches only that class tree (the class and its sub-classes) and declines when the OS gives no class or the class table is not valid; the hardware rule never reads the OS and searches all of cmdb_ci_hardware. A second CI outside the chosen class tree that shares the serial is invisible here, so the in-class CI is still returned, while the same pair makes the hardware rule decline.

rules.name: USEM Serial Number Hardware Match
rules.purpose: Second and last serial rule: the same serial search, but across the whole hardware tree (cmdb_ci_hardware and every class beneath it: servers, computers, network gear, storage, printers). It exists for hosts whose OS gives no usable class (unauthenticated scans listing several guesses) and for CIs that sit in a different class than the OS suggests; its only safety is that the serial must belong to exactly one CI in the whole tree.
rules.reads: SERIAL_NUMBER (sourceValue) only; the OS, IP and DNS fields of the payload are never read.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the single CI under cmdb_ci_hardware (any class beneath it, ignored classes excluded) whose serial_number equals the trimmed serial; null in every other case.
rules.before: USEM Serial Number Class Match already tried the serial inside the class the OS implies; hosts reach this rule because the OS gave no class (empty, no keyword, or three or more '/' guesses, as in the sample with seven), the class table was not valid, or the serial was absent or duplicated inside that class. Hosts with no serial or a placeholder serial were declined there and are declined here again by the same guards.
rules.after: USEM Cisco IP Phone MAC, then the name rules (USEM FQDN Class Match onwards); a serial that is not unique in the whole hardware tree is never used by any later rule.

rules.name: USEM Cisco IP Phone MAC
rules.purpose: Trusts the Cisco Unified CM device-name convention: the first DNS label is SEP followed by the phone's MAC address. It sits after the serial number rules (phones report no serial) and before the FQDN and hostname rules so a phone label is never tried as a server name; it searches only IP Phone CIs, so a MAC clash can never pull in a switch or a server.
rules.reads: DNS field as sourceValue (sample sep64f69dd5c9b0.voip.bankofamerica.com). No payload field is read: sourcePayload is received but never used. Also reads the framework variable _ignoreClass or, failing that, the property sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass.
rules.returns: The sys_id of exactly one cmdb_ci_ip_phone record (sub-classes included): the owner of a network adapter carrying the MAC, else the phone whose mac_address holds it, else the phone named with the device name upper-cased (SEP64F69DD5C9B0). null in every other case.
rules.before: USEM Serial Number Class Match and USEM Serial Number Hardware Match run first; phones report no serial number to the scan, so both decline and every phone host reaches this rule.
rules.after: The FQDN and hostname rules, starting with USEM FQDN Class Match; a null hands the host on unchanged. Hosts whose label is not sep plus twelve hex characters pass straight through.

mechanics.title: Empty guard.
mechanics.detail: Returns null at once when sourceValue (the DNS field) is empty. sourcePayload is never read: the rule works from the DNS name alone, so OS and IP play no part.

mechanics.title: Phone label test.
mechanics.detail: String-coerces the DNS value (no trim), takes the first label before the first dot and lower-cases it. The label must match ^sep([0-9a-f]{12})$ exactly: literal sep plus twelve hex characters; anything else (a server named sepulveda01) returns null.

mechanics.title: MAC rebuilt in four spellings.
mechanics.detail: The twelve hex characters are cut into six two-character pairs joined with colons. Four candidates are built in this order: colon form upper case, colon form lower case, plain hex upper case, plain hex lower case (64:F6:9D:D5:C9:B0 to 64f69dd5c9b0).

mechanics.title: Ignore list.
mechanics.detail: Reads the ignored classes from the framework variable _ignoreClass when defined and non-empty, otherwise from gs.getProperty sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass with an empty default. Applied to the second and third attempts only, not to the adapter attempt.

mechanics.title: Attempt 1: adapter owned by an IP phone.
mechanics.detail: Queries cmdb_ci_network_adapter where mac_address IN the four candidates and cmdb_ci is not empty. Each adapter's owner sys_id is tested with a GlideRecord get on cmdb_ci_ip_phone; distinct IP Phone owners are counted once each in a map.

mechanics.title: Attempt 1 decision.
mechanics.detail: Exactly one distinct IP Phone owner returns that owner's sys_id. Zero owners, or two or more phones sharing the MAC on adapters, fall through to the next attempt. An adapter owned by a switch or server is skipped because the get on cmdb_ci_ip_phone fails.

mechanics.title: Attempt 2: MAC on the phone record.
mechanics.detail: Queries cmdb_ci_ip_phone (sub-classes included) where mac_address IN the four candidates, with sys_class_name NOT IN the ignore list when it is non-empty. next() then hasNext(): one row returns its sys_id; none or several rows fall through to the name attempt.

mechanics.title: Attempt 3: Unified CM device name.
mechanics.detail: Queries cmdb_ci_ip_phone where name equals the label upper-cased (SEP64F69DD5C9B0), sys_class_name NOT IN the ignore list when non-empty. No row returns null; next() then hasNext() true returns null; one row returns its sys_id. No setLimit anywhere.

declines: sourceValue (DNS) is empty.
The lower-cased first DNS label does not match ^sep([0-9a-f]{12})$: not a Cisco Unified CM phone label; the host passes to the next rule untouched.
No IP Phone is found by adapter MAC, by the mac_address field or by the device name.
The name attempt finds two or more cmdb_ci_ip_phone records named with the device name (hasNext true).

mechanics.detail: pref = classFor(sourcePayload.OS): the lower-cased OS text matched on keywords gives a class (Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server 7.9 gives cmdb_ci_linux_server). An unknown OS or three or more '/'-separated guesses give '' and then nothing is refused on class.

mechanics.title: Query the DNS Name to IP Address link table.

mechanics.title: Walk every row and count distinct agreeing CIs.
mechanics.detail: All rows are read, no setLimit or hasNext. owner is ip_address.nic.cmdb_ci; a row failing agrees() is skipped, not counted or marked. Distinct owners count once, first kept. With ip set, a row whose ip_address.ip_address equals ip marks its owner in ipOwners.

mechanics.title: One CI: return it unless it is a load balancer.
mechanics.detail: When count is 1 the rule returns the first owner, but returns null when isLoadBalancer(first) finds that sys_id on cmdb_ci_lb: the name then belongs to a virtual address the balancer answers on, the host sits behind it and the load balancer rules take over.

mechanics.title: Several CIs: the scanned IP breaks the tie.
mechanics.detail: When count is above 1, confirmed = Object.keys(ipOwners). Exactly one CI reached through the scanned address, and not on cmdb_ci_lb, is returned. None, two or more, or a load balancer as the one confirmed CI gives null; no fitness heuristic is applied.

mechanics.title: No CI: decline.
mechanics.detail: count 0 (no DNS Name row for the name, no CI at the end of any chain, every CI on the ignore list, or every CI of a class the OS rules out) returns null and the host goes on to the next rule.

rules.sibling: Unlike USEM FQDN Class Match, USEM FQDN Hardware Match, USEM Hostname Domain Class Match and USEM Hostname Domain Hardware Match, which query a CI table (the class the OS implies, or cmdb_ci_hardware) on fqdn or name, walk every row and break a tie by the ip_address field of the CI record, and unlike USEM Hostname Class Match and USEM Hostname Hardware Match, which query name and decide exactly-one by next() then hasNext() with no tie-break, this rule queries cmdb_ip_address_dns_name and dot-walks to the CI: the OS class is never the queried table but a preference applied by agrees() to the CI reached (shared among the name rules only with USEM Hostname Hardware Match); an OS that gives no class does not decline here as it does in the Class rules; the tie is broken by ip_address.ip_address on the IP Address record in the chain; an alias resolves to the real machine; and a load balancer device at the end of the chain is refused, which no other name rule does. rules.name: USEM Hostname Class Match
rules.purpose: Trusts the short hostname (first DNS label) only inside the CMDB class the scanned OS implies, so the OS-to-class agreement stands in for the domain evidence the CI lacks. rules.before: Every rule ahead of it needed domain evidence on the CI (a match on fqdn, dns_domain or the discovery DNS records); they decline a CI that carries only a short name and no domain information, which is exactly the host this rule reaches.
rules.after: USEM Hostname Hardware Match (then USEM FQDN Name Hardware Match for CIs named with the full FQDN)

mechanics.title: Refuse a load balancer.

mechanics.title: Walk the prefixes, longest first.
mechanics.detail: k runs from segments.length - 1 down to 1; base is the first k segments joined by '-'. The full label is never tried, and the single first segment is the last prefix tried. Sample order: '...-cz04-hsrp', '...-cz04', 'uspaltwrr01drm0119'.

mechanics.title: Decide at the first prefix that finds anything.

mechanics.title: Exhausted walk.
mechanics.detail: When no prefix down to the first segment names any Network Gear or Load Balancer record, the loop ends and the rule returns null; the host passes to USEM FQDN Name Hardware Match.

rules.name: USEM FQDN Name Broad Match
rules.purpose: The last USEM rule and the only one that searches the root cmdb_ci table: a CI whose name is the complete scanned FQDN in any class (a virtual machine instance or another logical CI), still requiring a single row outside the ignored classes. It runs last so every more precise rule has had its chance.
rules.reads: Source field DNS (sourceValue). No payload field is read: neither IP nor OS influences the result.
rules.returns: The sys_id of the single cmdb_ci row, in any class not on the ignore list, whose name equals the scanned FQDN; null when none or the name is shared.
rules.before: Every hardware-scoped USEM rule declined for this host, including USEM FQDN Name Hardware Match, which searched the same full-FQDN name but only under cmdb_ci_hardware, and the IP rules USEM IP Class Match, USEM IP Hardware Match, USEM IP Adapter Match and USEM IP Layered Match.
rules.after: The out-of-box Qualys rules: Qualys Host ID, Cloud Resource Id, FQDN, NetBIOS and DNS (the out-of-box IP rules are inactive by default). No USEM rule follows.

mechanics.title: Guard and normalise the DNS value.
mechanics.detail: Returns null when sourceValue is empty or absent. Otherwise coerces it to a string, trims it and lower-cases it. The whole dotted string is kept: no first label is cut and no domain suffix is stripped.

mechanics.title: Require a dotted name.
mechanics.detail: Returns null when the normalised value contains no '.' character; a bare label is left to the hostname rules.

mechanics.title: Build the ignored-class list.
mechanics.detail: ignore is '' + _ignoreClass when that global is defined and truthy, otherwise gs.getProperty('sn_sec_cmn.ignoreCIClass', ''). When non-empty it becomes the query condition sys_class_name NOT IN that comma-separated list.

mechanics.title: Query the root cmdb_ci table on name.
mechanics.detail: GlideRecord('cmdb_ci'), addQuery('name', normalised FQDN), the NOT IN ignore condition when set, then query(). Every class is searched, hardware and logical alike; only the ignore list keeps placeholder classes out. No setLimit, no isValid() guard.

mechanics.title: Take the first row with next().
mechanics.detail: If gr.next() is false the rule returns null. Otherwise match holds gr.getUniqueValue() of that first row.

mechanics.title: Reject a second row with hasNext().
mechanics.detail: If gr.hasNext() is true a second CI of any class carries the same name and the rule returns null; the scanned IP, the class or a retired status never break the tie.

mechanics.title: Return the single match.
mechanics.detail: match is returned only when the query produced exactly one row. No IP tie-break, OS class, retired test or twin grouping exists in this script.

declines: sourceValue is empty or absent
the normalised DNS value contains no '.' (a bare hostname)
no cmdb_ci row outside the ignored classes has name equal to the scanned FQDN
two or more cmdb_ci rows share that name (gr.hasNext() true), whatever their class, IP or status
